questions.knowledge_point: Using Alternative Forms of Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Expressions
questions.problem: Express $2{cos}^{2}⁡{45}^{∘}-1$ as a single trigonometric ratio.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
2{cos}^{2}⁡x-1=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x={45}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{cos}^{2}⁡{45}^{∘}-1 & =\operatorname{cos}⁡2\cdot {45}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡{90}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Express $2{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3})-1$ as a single trigonometric ratio.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
2{cos}^{2}⁡x-1=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{5\pi }{3}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3})-1 & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{5\pi }{3}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{10\pi }{3}).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Exact Values of Trigonometric Expressions Using the Double-Angle Formula
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x={165}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡{165}^{∘}-{sin}^{2}⁡{165}^{∘} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot {165}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡{330}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Exact Values of Trigonometric Expressions Using the Double-Angle Formula
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that our expression is a perfect square that can be rewritten as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{4}⁡({15}^{∘})-2{cos}^{2}⁡({15}^{∘}){sin}^{2}⁡({15}^{∘})+{sin}^{4}⁡({15}^{∘}) & ={({cos}^{2}⁡({15}^{∘})-{sin}^{2}⁡({15}^{∘}))}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x={15}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡({15}^{∘})-{sin}^{2}⁡({15}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot {15}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡({30}^{∘}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{({cos}^{2}⁡({15}^{∘})-{sin}^{2}⁡({15}^{∘}))}^{2} & ={(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}^{2}=\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Exact Values of Trigonometric Expressions Using the Double-Angle Formula
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that our expression is a perfect square that can be rewritten as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{4}⁡({67.5}^{∘})-2{cos}^{2}⁡({67.5}^{∘}){sin}^{2}⁡({67.5}^{∘})+{sin}^{4}⁡({67.5}^{∘}) & ={({cos}^{2}⁡({67.5}^{∘})-{sin}^{2}⁡({67.5}^{∘}))}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x={67.5}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡({67.5}^{∘})-{sin}^{2}⁡({67.5}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot {67.5}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡({135}^{∘}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{({cos}^{2}⁡({67.5}^{∘})-{sin}^{2}⁡({67.5}^{∘}))}^{2} & ={(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
